stocks.name: Apple
stocks.summary: Apple is trading just 0.8% below its 52‑week high and 38.5% above its low, with modest recent weakness (-0.8% today) after a solid 7.6% month and 25.2% YTD gain. The stock is near the top of its range, so investors should watch any catalyst that could push it to new highs, such as upcoming product launches or earnings guidance.

stocks.name: Microsoft
stocks.summary: Microsoft sits 5.3% shy of its 52‑week peak and 44.6% above its low, after a mixed week but a modest 0.8% rise this month and 8.4% YTD growth. With the price near the upper band, the next focus is the company’s quarterly results and cloud spending trends.

stocks.name: NVIDIA
stocks.summary: NVIDIA is 2.7% below its 52‑week high and 38.9% above its low, posting modest gains across all time frames and a 21.5% YTD rise. Investors should monitor GPU demand and AI spending outlook as the stock hovers near its recent highs.

stocks.name: Alphabet
stocks.summary: Alphabet trades 14.8% below its 52‑week high and 45.3% above its low, after a slight dip today and a 9.0% YTD increase. The key watch point is the impact of AI initiatives and ad‑revenue trends as the stock remains mid‑range.

stocks.name: Amazon
stocks.summary: Amazon is 13.3% under its 52‑week high but 23.8% above its low, with recent declines across the week and a modest 8.7% YTD gain. Focus will be on retail traffic and cloud growth ahead of the next earnings report.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms
stocks.summary: Meta Platforms sits 8.0% below its 52‑week high and 36.4% above its low, after a sharp 4.8% drop today but a strong 25.4% month and 10.3% YTD rise. Investors should watch user growth and ad‑revenue trends, especially after recent earnings volatility.

stocks.name: Tesla
stocks.summary: Tesla is 27.0% off its 52‑week high yet only 19.8% above its low, with a down‑trend this week and a -18.4% YTD performance. The next catalyst is production and delivery guidance, plus any news on pricing or new model rollouts.

stocks.name: Broadcom
stocks.summary: Broadcom trades 27.2% below its 52‑week high and 19.5% above its low, slipping across the week and posting a modest 1.1% YTD gain. Investors should watch the semiconductor demand outlook and any updates on its recent acquisitions.

stocks.name: Advanced Micro Devices
stocks.summary: AMD is just 3.6% below its 52‑week high while soaring 276.7% above its low, delivering a massive 172% YTD surge and a strong 27.5% month. The key focus is whether the momentum can be sustained through upcoming earnings and competitive pressure in the GPU/CPU markets.

stocks.name: Oracle
stocks.summary: Oracle has slipped to $132.60, down 12.7% over the month and 31.6% YTD, now sitting 57.2% below its 52‑week high but 15.3% above its low. The recent sell‑off reflects cloud‑spending concerns; watch next week’s earnings guidance for signs of a turnaround.

stocks.name: Salesforce
stocks.summary: Salesforce is trading at $227.27, off 9.7% month‑to‑date and 9.8% YTD, roughly 14% under its 52‑week peak while still 51.7% above its low. Momentum remains negative; investors should focus on the upcoming quarterly revenue beat and AI‑driven product rollout.

stocks.name: JPMorgan Chase
stocks.summary: JPMorgan Chase sits at $336.59, down 5% over the month but up 4.9% YTD, 7.8% below its 52‑week high and 20.2% above its low. The stock is stabilizing after rate‑sensitivity pressure; watch net interest income trends in the next earnings report.

stocks.name: Bank of America
stocks.summary: Bank of America trades at $55.47, down 8.9% month‑to‑date and barely up 0.7% YTD, 14% under its 52‑week high and 20% above its low. Credit‑quality metrics and Fed policy cues will be key drivers ahead of its earnings call.

stocks.name: Visa
stocks.summary: Visa is at $367.74, down 3.1% over the month but up 6.8% YTD, only 4.3% shy of its 52‑week high and 24.9% above its low. Look for transaction‑volume trends and any shifts in consumer spending patterns as the next catalyst.

stocks.name: Mastercard
stocks.summary: Mastercard trades at $568.26, down 4% month‑to‑date and up 1.4% YTD, 5.3% below its 52‑week peak and 20.7% above its low. Investor focus should be on cross‑border volume recovery and the impact of emerging‑market pricing pressure.

stocks.name: Netflix
stocks.summary: Netflix sits at $69.23, down 13.3% in the past month and 23.9% YTD, 44.2% below its 52‑week high but just 2.4% above its low. The key watch is subscriber growth and content spend efficiency ahead of the next earnings release.

stocks.name: Eli Lilly
stocks.summary: Eli Lilly is trading at $1,184.78, up 0.7% month‑to‑date and 10.2% YTD, 7.5% under its 52‑week high while still 64.1% above its low. Watch upcoming FDA decisions and diabetes pipeline updates for forward momentum.

stocks.name: UnitedHealth
stocks.summary: UnitedHealth shares are at $377.83, down 3.8% over the month but up 14.5% YTD, 12.9% below its 52‑week high and 47.6% above its low. The next focus is on medical‑cost trend guidance and enrollment growth in its Medicare Advantage business.

stocks.name: Johnson & Johnson
stocks.summary: Johnson & Johnson has nudged up 0.3% today and is still 2.3% below its 52‑week high, sitting roughly halfway between its extremes after a strong 33.3% YTD gain. The modest daily uptick follows a broader uptrend, but investors should watch upcoming earnings guidance for signs of sustained growth.

stocks.name: Walmart
stocks.summary: Walmart rose 0.7% on the day, remaining 18.8% off its 52‑week peak while still 9.0% above its low, reflecting a modest recovery after a 3% YTD dip. The key catalyst to monitor is same‑store sales trends as the retailer navigates inflation pressures.

stocks.name: Costco
stocks.summary: Costco is flat today, trading 15.5% below its 52‑week high and 9.1% above its low after a mixed month and an 8.5% YTD rise. Investors should focus on membership renewal rates and any shifts in discretionary spending that could impact its margin profile.

stocks.name: Home Depot
stocks.summary: Home Depot slipped 1.1% and is now 26.7% under its 52‑week high, essentially at its 52‑week low after a 14.4% YTD decline. The next inflection point will be the upcoming housing market data and its effect on DIY demand.

stocks.name: Exxon Mobil
stocks.summary: Exxon Mobil gained 1.2% today, trading 4.0% below its 52‑week high while still 51.1% above its low, buoyed by a 35.2% YTD rally. Investors should keep an eye on crude price trends and the company’s capital‑allocation plans.

stocks.name: Coca-Cola
stocks.summary: Coca‑Cola slipped 0.7% but stays 4.7% under its 52‑week high and 35.5% above its low, after a solid 28.6% YTD increase. The key watch is the beverage segment’s volume growth amid shifting consumer preferences.

stocks.name: Walt Disney
stocks.summary: Disney fell 0.5% on the day, now 8.2% below its 52‑week high and 15.1% above its low after a 4.9% YTD decline. The primary focus will be the performance of its streaming services and the rollout of its new park attractions.
